header:
import Mathlib
open scoped TensorProduct
noncomputable section
namespace Chevalley
def R (p : ℕ) : Subalgebra ℤ ℚ :=
  Algebra.adjoin ℤ {q : ℚ | ∃ b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (b : ℚ)⁻¹}
instance rComplex (p : ℕ) : Algebra (R p) ℂ :=
  Algebra.compHom ℂ (algebraMap (R p) ℚ)
variable {V : Type} [AddCommGroup V] [Module ℂ V]
def dp (f : Module.End ℂ V) (r : ℕ) : Module.End ℂ V :=
  ((r.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹) • f ^ r
def e (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) : V := dp y i v
abbrev MR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) := (R p) ⊗[ℤ] M
def mu (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : MR p M → V :=
  letI := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
  letI : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def image (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Set V := Set.range (mu p M)
def latticeOp (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Module.End ℤ M :=
  letI := Classical.propDecidable
  if hf : ∀ u ∈ M, f u ∈ M then (f.restrictScalars ℤ).restrict hf else 0
abbrev VK (K : Type) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) := K ⊗[ℤ] M
def opK (K : Type) [Field K] (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) :
    Module.End K (VK K M) := (latticeOp M f).baseChange K
def unitOp {F W : Type} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    {ι : Type} (b : Module.Basis ι F W) (i j : ι) : Module.End F W :=
  (b.coord j).smulRight (b i)
def muR (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) :
    letI := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
    MR p M →ₗ[R p] V :=
  letI := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
  letI : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
  M.subtype.liftBaseChange (R p)
def J (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) (i : ℕ) :
    Submodule (R p) ℂ :=
  letI := Module.compHom V (algebraMap (R p) ℂ)
  letI : IsScalarTower (R p) ℂ V := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℂ V
  (muR p M).range.comap (LinearMap.smulRight (LinearMap.id : ℂ →ₗ[R p] ℂ) (e y v i))
def QJ (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
    Submodule ℚ ℂ := Submodule.span ℚ (J p M y v 0 : Set ℂ)
def qmul (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (y : Module.End ℂ V) (v : V) :
    ℚ ⊗[R p] (J p M y v 0) →ₗ[ℚ] ℂ :=
  letI := IsScalarTower.of_compHom (R p) ℚ ℂ
  (J p M y v 0).subtype.liftBaseChange ℚ
abbrev Index (ell : ℤ) := Fin (ell.toNat + 1)
def stable {F W : Type} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    (U : Submodule F W) (f : Module.End F W) : Prop := ∀ w ∈ U, f w ∈ U
def inImage (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ image p M, f w ∈ image p M
def preserves (M : Submodule ℤ V) (f : Module.End ℂ V) : Prop :=
  ∀ w ∈ M, f w ∈ M
def reductions (K : Type) [Field K] (p : ℕ) (M : Submodule ℤ V) : Prop :=
  ∃ hc : CharP K p,
  letI := hc
  letI := ZMod.algebra K p
  ∃ ρ : R p →+* K,
  (∀ a : ℤ, ρ (a : R p) = (a : K)) ∧
  letI := ρ.toAlgebra
  ∃ Φ : VK K M ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[R p] MR p M),
    (∀ (c : K) (m : M), Φ (c ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m) = c ⊗ₜ[R p] ((1 : R p) ⊗ₜ[ℤ] m)) ∧
    ∃ Ψ : (K ⊗[R p] MR p M) ≃ₗ[K] (K ⊗[ZMod p] ModN (MR p M) p),
      ∀ (c : K) (u : MR p M), Ψ (c ⊗ₜ[R p] u) = c ⊗ₜ[ZMod p] ModN.mkQ p u
def basisVec {F W : Type} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    {n : ℕ} (b : Module.Basis (Fin n) F W) (i : ℕ) : W :=
  if hi : i < n then b ⟨i, hi⟩ else 0
def stringActions {F W : Type} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    (ell : ℤ) (x y h : Module.End F W) (a : ℕ → W) : Prop :=
  ∀ i : ℕ, i ≤ ell.toNat →
    x (a i) = (if i = 0 then 0 else ((ell - (i : ℤ) + 1 : ℤ) : F) • a (i - 1)) ∧
    y (a i) = (if i < ell.toNat then ((i + 1 : ℕ) : F) • a (i + 1) else 0) ∧
    h (a i) = ((ell - 2 * (i : ℤ) : ℤ) : F) • a i
def dividedActions {F W : Type} [Field F] [AddCommGroup W] [Module F W]
    (ell : ℤ) (X Y : ℕ → Module.End F W) (a : ℕ → W) : Prop :=
  ∀ (r i : ℕ), i ≤ ell.toNat →
    X r (a i) = (if r ≤ i then ((Nat.choose (ell.toNat - i + r) r : ℕ) : F) • a (i - r) else 0) ∧
    Y r (a i) = (if i + r ≤ ell.toNat then ((Nat.choose (i + r) r : ℕ) : F) • a (i + r) else 0)
def matrixK (K : Type) [Field K] (ell : ℤ) (M : Submodule ℤ V)
    (x y : Module.End ℂ V) (i j : Index ell) : Module.End K (VK K M) :=
  ((Nat.choose ell.toNat j.val : K)⁻¹) •
    (opK K M (dp x (ell.toNat - i.val)) *
      (opK K M (dp y ell.toNat) * opK K M (dp x ell.toNat)) *
        opK K M (dp y (ell.toNat - j.val)))
end Chevalley

premise_types.H001: p.Prime ∧ CharP K p ∧ 0 ≤ ell ∧ ell < (p : ℤ)
premise_types.H002: FiniteDimensional ℂ V ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = ell.toNat + 1 ∧ h * x - x * h = (2 : ℂ) • x ∧ h * y - y * h = (-2 : ℂ) • y ∧ x * y - y * x = h ∧ (∃ w : V, w ≠ 0 ∧ x w = 0 ∧ h w = (ell : ℂ) • w) ∧ (∀ W : Submodule ℂ V, Chevalley.stable W x → Chevalley.stable W y → Chevalley.stable W h → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤)
premise_types.H003: v ≠ 0 ∧ x v = 0 ∧ h v = (ell : ℂ) • v
premise_types.H004: (∃ (d : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℤ M) (B : Module.Basis (Fin d) ℂ V), ∀ i, (b i : V) = B i) ∧ (∀ r : ℕ, Chevalley.preserves M (Chevalley.dp x r) ∧ Chevalley.preserves M (Chevalley.dp y r))

conclusion_type: Nontrivial (Chevalley.VK K M) ∧ ∀ W : Submodule K (Chevalley.VK K M), Chevalley.stable W (Chevalley.opK K M x) → Chevalley.stable W (Chevalley.opK K M y) → Chevalley.stable W (Chevalley.opK K M h) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
representation: Use the actual complex representation via its three complex-linear Chevalley operators; their commutator relations specify an sl2 action. p is natural because every integer prime in the source is positive; ell remains an integer and ell.toNat is used only under H001's 0≤ell. Index ell=Fin(ell.toNat+1) is the endpoint-inclusive source I via i↦(i.val:ℤ). M is a Z-submodule of V, equivalent to an additive subgroup. The rational localization R is the Z-subalgebra of Q generated by reciprocals of all integers not divisible by p; T005 proves its precise fraction description rather than assuming it. Tensor products are left scalar extensions R⊗Z M and K⊗Z M. mu is scalar multiplication, and J is the exact coordinate inverse image of its range. qmul is the actual multiplication map into C, never an abstract rank surrogate. The endomorphism restriction latticeOp is defined by restriction when preservation holds and zero otherwise; T005 proves preservation so all operators used in the theorem are the genuine induced lattice maps. Library instance constructors in definitions provide only canonical scalar restrictions. They assert no unproved mathematical properties.

steps.explanation: Induct on natural exponents using the two Chevalley commutators; natural exponents identify exactly with the source nonnegative integer exponents.

steps.statement: ∃ b : Module.Basis (Chevalley.Index ell) ℂ V, ∀ i, b i = Chevalley.e y v i.val
steps.explanation: Show each divided lowering vector is nonzero; distinct complex h-eigenvalues give independence by the source annihilating polynomial argument, and the given dimension gives a basis.

steps.statement: (∀ t : ℕ, ell.toNat < t → (y ^ t) v = 0) ∧ Chevalley.stringActions ell x y h (Chevalley.e y v) ∧ Chevalley.dividedActions ell (Chevalley.dp x) (Chevalley.dp y) (Chevalley.e y v)
steps.explanation: Use the forbidden terminal weight in the established basis to prove termination, then compute generator and divided-power matrices by iteration. Natural binomial coefficients encode integrality.

steps.statement: 0 < ell.toNat + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Chevalley.Index ell) = ell.toNat + 1 ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = ell.toNat + 1 ∧ ((∀ t : ℕ, h ((y ^ t) v) = ((ell : ℂ) - 2 * (t : ℂ)) • ((y ^ t) v)) ∧ (∀ t : ℕ, 0 < t → x ((y ^ t) v) = ((t : ℂ) * ((ell : ℂ) - (t : ℂ) + 1)) • ((y ^ (t - 1)) v))) ∧ (∃ b : Module.Basis (Chevalley.Index ell) ℂ V, ∀ i, b i = Chevalley.e y v i.val) ∧ ((∀ t : ℕ, ell.toNat < t → (y ^ t) v = 0) ∧ Chevalley.stringActions ell x y h (Chevalley.e y v) ∧ Chevalley.dividedActions ell (Chevalley.dp x) (Chevalley.dp y) (Chevalley.e y v))
steps.explanation: Package N001, keeping all power identities, dimension, basis, termination and integral matrix formulas.

steps.statement: (∀ q : ℚ, q ∈ Chevalley.R p ↔ ∃ a b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)) ∧ Function.Injective (Chevalley.mu p M) ∧ Nonempty (Module.Basis (Chevalley.Index ell) (Chevalley.R p) (Chevalley.MR p M)) ∧ Submodule.span ℂ (Chevalley.image p M) = ⊤ ∧ (∀ r : ℕ, Chevalley.inImage p M (Chevalley.dp x r) ∧ Chevalley.inImage p M (Chevalley.dp y r)) ∧ Chevalley.preserves M x ∧ Chevalley.preserves M y ∧ Chevalley.preserves M h ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (u : Chevalley.MR p M), Chevalley.mu p M (((Chevalley.latticeOp M (Chevalley.dp x r)).baseChange (Chevalley.R p)) u) = Chevalley.dp x r (Chevalley.mu p M u) ∧ Chevalley.mu p M (((Chevalley.latticeOp M (Chevalley.dp y r)).baseChange (Chevalley.R p)) u) = Chevalley.dp y r (Chevalley.mu p M u))
steps.explanation: Identify the adjoin ring with the specified rational localization, reindex an admissible integer basis, and extend it to prove injectivity, freeness, spanning and operator stability/intertwining. Use Mathlib basis base change directly.

steps.statement: ((∀ q : ℚ, q ∈ Chevalley.R p ↔ ∃ a b : ℤ, ¬ (p : ℤ) ∣ b ∧ q = (a : ℚ) / (b : ℚ)) ∧ Function.Injective (Chevalley.mu p M) ∧ Nonempty (Module.Basis (Chevalley.Index ell) (Chevalley.R p) (Chevalley.MR p M)) ∧ Submodule.span ℂ (Chevalley.image p M) = ⊤ ∧ (∀ r : ℕ, Chevalley.inImage p M (Chevalley.dp x r) ∧ Chevalley.inImage p M (Chevalley.dp y r)) ∧ Chevalley.preserves M x ∧ Chevalley.preserves M y ∧ Chevalley.preserves M h ∧ (∀ (r : ℕ) (u : Chevalley.MR p M), Chevalley.mu p M (((Chevalley.latticeOp M (Chevalley.dp x r)).baseChange (Chevalley.R p)) u) = Chevalley.dp x r (Chevalley.mu p M u) ∧ Chevalley.mu p M (((Chevalley.latticeOp M (Chevalley.dp y r)).baseChange (Chevalley.R p)) u) = Chevalley.dp y r (Chevalley.mu p M u))) ∧ (∀ (b : Module.Basis (Chevalley.Index ell) ℂ V), (∀ i, b i = Chevalley.e y v i.val) → ∀ i j : Chevalley.Index ell, IsUnit (Nat.choose ell.toNat j.val : Chevalley.R p) ∧ Chevalley.dp y ell.toNat * Chevalley.dp x ell.toNat = Chevalley.unitOp b (Fin.last ell.toNat) (Fin.last ell.toNat) ∧ Chevalley.dp x (ell.toNat - i.val) * (Chevalley.dp y ell.toNat * Chevalley.dp x ell.toNat) = Chevalley.unitOp b i (Fin.last ell.toNat) ∧ (Chevalley.dp y ell.toNat * Chevalley.dp x ell.toNat) * Chevalley.dp y (ell.toNat - j.val) = (Nat.choose ell.toNat j.val : ℂ) • Chevalley.unitOp b (Fin.last ell.toNat) j ∧ Chevalley.unitOp b i j = ((Nat.choose ell.toNat j.val : ℂ)⁻¹) • (Chevalley.dp x (ell.toNat - i.val) * (Chevalley.dp y ell.toNat * Chevalley.dp x ell.toNat) * Chevalley.dp y (ell.toNat - j.val)) ∧ Chevalley.inImage p M (Chevalley.unitOp b i j))
steps.explanation: Evaluate the endpoint composites on the string basis, prove binomial units from ell<p, and deduce each matrix unit preserves the localized image. Include T005 as N002's full lattice assertions.

steps.statement: (∀ i : Chevalley.Index ell, Chevalley.J p M y v i.val = Chevalley.J p M y v 0) ∧ (Chevalley.J p M y v 0).FG ∧ Chevalley.J p M y v 0 ≠ ⊥ ∧ (∀ u : V, u ∈ Chevalley.image p M ↔ ∃! c : Chevalley.Index ell → ℂ, (∀ i, c i ∈ Chevalley.J p M y v 0) ∧ u = ∑ i, c i • Chevalley.e y v i.val)
steps.explanation: Coordinate projections and matrix units identify all Ji, prove finite generation and nonzero, and yield the unique internal coordinate decomposition.

steps.statement: Function.Injective (Chevalley.qmul p M y v) ∧ LinearMap.range (Chevalley.qmul p M y v) = Chevalley.QJ p M y v ∧ FiniteDimensional ℚ (ℚ ⊗[Chevalley.R p] (Chevalley.J p M y v 0)) ∧ FiniteDimensional ℚ (Chevalley.QJ p M y v)
steps.explanation: Prove Q is the fraction localization of R and QJ is the localized coefficient module by denominator clearing; the multiplication map is injective and has exactly QJ as its range. Resolve Mathlib's localized-module/base-change API locally.

steps.statement: Nonempty ((ℚ ⊗[Chevalley.R p] Chevalley.MR p M) ≃ₗ[ℚ] (Chevalley.Index ell → (ℚ ⊗[Chevalley.R p] (Chevalley.J p M y v 0))))
steps.explanation: Extend the coordinate and insertion maps across tensor products, checking both inverse identities on pure tensors.

steps.statement: ((∀ i : Chevalley.Index ell, Chevalley.J p M y v i.val = Chevalley.J p M y v 0) ∧ (Chevalley.J p M y v 0).FG ∧ Chevalley.J p M y v 0 ≠ ⊥ ∧ (∀ u : V, u ∈ Chevalley.image p M ↔ ∃! c : Chevalley.Index ell → ℂ, (∀ i, c i ∈ Chevalley.J p M y v 0) ∧ u = ∑ i, c i • Chevalley.e y v i.val)) ∧ (Function.Injective (Chevalley.qmul p M y v) ∧ LinearMap.range (Chevalley.qmul p M y v) = Chevalley.QJ p M y v ∧ FiniteDimensional ℚ (ℚ ⊗[Chevalley.R p] (Chevalley.J p M y v 0)) ∧ FiniteDimensional ℚ (Chevalley.QJ p M y v)) ∧ (Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[Chevalley.R p] Chevalley.MR p M) = ell.toNat + 1 ∧ ell.toNat + 1 = (ell.toNat + 1) * Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[Chevalley.R p] (Chevalley.J p M y v 0)) ∧ Module.finrank ℚ (ℚ ⊗[Chevalley.R p] (Chevalley.J p M y v 0)) = 1 ∧ Module.finrank ℚ (Chevalley.QJ p M y v) = 1)
steps.explanation: Compute rational dimensions of the localized lattice and its finite coordinate product using library basis base change and product finrank. Cancel the positive string length to obtain rank one and package all of N003.

steps.statement: ∃ b : ℂ, b ∈ Chevalley.J p M y v 0 ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧ Chevalley.J p M y v 0 = Submodule.span (Chevalley.R p) ({b} : Set ℂ)
steps.explanation: Choose a nonzero coefficient, express finitely many generators on its rational line, and use a generator with minimal p-exponent to prove principality exactly as in the accepted proof.

steps.statement: ∃ b : ℂ, b ∈ Chevalley.J p M y v 0 ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧ Chevalley.J p M y v 0 = Submodule.span (Chevalley.R p) ({b} : Set ℂ) ∧ (∀ u : V, u ∈ Chevalley.image p M ↔ ∃ c : Chevalley.Index ell → Chevalley.R p, u = ∑ i, (algebraMap (Chevalley.R p) ℂ (c i)) • (b • Chevalley.e y v i.val)) ∧ ∃ B : Module.Basis (Chevalley.Index ell) (Chevalley.R p) (Chevalley.MR p M), ∀ i, Chevalley.mu p M (B i) = b • Chevalley.e y v i.val ∧ (∀ u, Chevalley.mu p M u = b • Chevalley.e y v i.val → u = B i)
steps.explanation: Substitute J=Rb in the internal decomposition, prove independence of b times the string basis, and pull this basis back uniquely through mu to obtain N004.

Construct the denominator map R→K and the two natural scalar-extension/reduction equivalences with the displayed pure-tensor formulas. ModN is the actual quotient by p-multiples, not a new ambient module.

steps.statement: 0 < ell.toNat + 1 ∧ Fintype.card (Chevalley.Index ell) = ell.toNat + 1 ∧ (Chevalley.reductions K p M) ∧ (∃ β : Module.Basis (Chevalley.Index ell) K (Chevalley.VK K M), Chevalley.stringActions ell (Chevalley.opK K M x) (Chevalley.opK K M y) (Chevalley.opK K M h) (Chevalley.basisVec β) ∧ Chevalley.dividedActions ell (fun r => Chevalley.opK K M (Chevalley.dp x r)) (fun r => Chevalley.opK K M (Chevalley.dp y r)) (Chevalley.basisVec β) ∧ (∀ r : ℕ, r ≤ ell.toNat → (r.factorial : K) ≠ 0 ∧ Chevalley.opK K M (Chevalley.dp x r) = ((r.factorial : K)⁻¹) • Chevalley.opK K M x ^ r ∧ Chevalley.opK K M (Chevalley.dp y r) = ((r.factorial : K)⁻¹) • Chevalley.opK K M y ^ r) ∧ (∀ i j : Chevalley.Index ell, (Nat.choose ell.toNat j.val : K) ≠ 0 ∧ Chevalley.matrixK K ell M x y i j = Chevalley.unitOp β i j) ∧ (∀ W : Submodule K (Chevalley.VK K M), Chevalley.stable W (Chevalley.opK K M x) → Chevalley.stable W (Chevalley.opK K M y) → ∀ i j, Chevalley.stable W (Chevalley.matrixK K ell M x y i j)))
steps.explanation: Extend the common-scalar lattice basis to K using the natural maps, transfer integer matrices and endpoint composites, and prove all factorial inverses and stability under the resulting matrix units. Package all of N005 including reduction equivalences.

steps.statement: Nontrivial (Chevalley.VK K M) ∧ ∀ W : Submodule K (Chevalley.VK K M), Chevalley.stable W (Chevalley.opK K M x) → Chevalley.stable W (Chevalley.opK K M y) → Chevalley.stable W (Chevalley.opK K M h) → W = ⊥ ∨ W = ⊤
steps.explanation: A nonzero invariant subspace has a nonzero coordinate; matrix units and inversion of that coordinate put every basis vector inside it. Positive basis length gives nontriviality. Generator invariance is precisely invariance for their K-linear Lie span, including characteristic two.

P.explanation: All original data remain arbitrary: a prime p, any characteristic-p field K, integer 0≤ell<p, an irreducible complex highest-weight module of the given dimension, its chosen highest vector, and any admissible lattice. H002 expresses the sl2 representation by complex-linear generators with exactly its three defining commutators, the stated dimension, highest-weight-vector existence and irreducibility under those generators; H003 fixes the chosen vector. H004 is exactly a simultaneous integer/complex basis plus stability under every divided power, equivalent to stability under the Z-algebra they generate. An additive subgroup is uniquely a Z-submodule. Positive integer primes are encoded by Nat primes; Index identifies with 0≤i≤ell. The canonical tensor flip identifies K⊗Z M with the source M⊗Z K, intertwining the induced operators. T005 proves restriction is in its preservation branch. Nontrivial means the vector space is nonzero, and forall Submodule with bottom/top says exactly every K-linear subspace stable under x,y,h is zero or the whole space. This is equivalent in both directions to invariance under their K-linear Lie span. No algebraic closure, p>2, positive ell or special lattice is assumed. ModN used in N005 is the actual quotient by p multiples, and its two equivalences are required with their natural generator formulas.
